new_findings.title: Pinned resolved executable is verified but dispatch resolves the original bare executable name again
new_findings.scenario: On Windows, copy host Python executable to temporary A/reviewpython.exe and B/reviewpython.exe. Append inert executable-overlay bytes to B, giving B a distinct SHA256 while retaining a runnable Python executable. Seal with PATH preferring A. Change PATH to prefer B and call the release. PYTHONHOME points to the existing host runtime so copied interpreters find their standard library.
new_findings.observed: seal records A path and hash. release verifies A. call succeeds with original bare command reviewpython.exe, which now resolves B; B hash differs from sealed executable hash. This independently reproduced twice. No malicious capsule code, sandbox violation, or process race is required.
new_findings.minimal_general_fix: Use the manifest-resolved executable path as actual native argv[0] after verifying it, or reject when the currently resolved executable differs from the sealed identity. For a bundle-contained executable, use its corresponding verified sealed copy. Record the actual path/hash dispatched, not only host self.python. Keep ordinary ambient dependency limitations explicit.
